mainTopic: פרשת שקלים: its timing and content, and how to divide the Torah readings when special days coincide
overview: The amud opens by explaining why the half-שקלים are announced on the first of אדר. According to רבי טבי, the קרבנות must be bought from the new collection starting in ניסן, and the money-changers' tables open on the fifteenth of אדר. Then רב and שמואל argue about which passage is פרשת שקלים: רב says the offerings passage, 'את קרבני לחמי', and שמואל says 'כי תשא'. The גמרא tests both views several times: the name of the reading, the purpose of the money, how ראש חודש אדר differs from other ראשי חדשים, the הפטרה of יהוידע הכהן, and when the passage comes up in the yearly cycle. Each test is answered, and a ברייתא supports שמואל. רבי יצחק נפחא rules that three ספרי תורה are used when ראש חודש אדר or ראש חודש טבת falls on שבת. On a weekday ראש חודש טבת, the הלכה is that three people read ראש חודש and one reads חנוכה. The amud ends with a new case, שקלים falling on the week of תצוה, and אביי's response begins on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the quoted משנה about mixed plantings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה: on the first of אדר, an announcement is also made about כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And an announcement is made about mixed plantings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of a משנה that lists announcements made on the first of אדר: one about the שקלים and one about כלאים. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה (שקלים 1:1) says that on the first of אדר, the בית דין announces about the שקלים and about כלאים. Both announcements are tied to the same date. The גמרא will now check whether each one really belongs at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures of seeds or plants growing together in a field
We announce publicly (the verb that this phrase continues from the משנה)

phrases.english: And about the mixed plantings.
phrases.notes: The end of the משנה's line: 'On the first of אדר we announce about the שקלים and about כלאים.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the משנה in שקלים that the sugya is building on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first of אדר, the בית דין announces about the שקלים and about uprooting כלאים.

steps.title: כלאים make sense in אדר, but why the שקלים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the כלאים announcement fits אדר because it is planting season. It asks why the שקלים announcement is also made then.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that we announce about כלאים, because it is planting time. But about the שקלים, how do we know it should be then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. One announcement has an obvious reason for its timing, so why is the other one made at the same time?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אדר, plants are coming up, so forbidden mixtures can already be noticed and uprooted. The שקלים have no link to farming seasons. So the גמרא wants a source or reason for announcing them specifically in אדר.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (accepting one side before asking about the other)
Planting season
The half-shekel coins every Jew gave yearly to fund communal קרבנות
From where do we know?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not challenging the כלאים announcement at all. It accepts it completely. The only question is about the timing of the שקלים announcement.

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding the mixed plantings,
since it is planting time,
phrases.notes: In early אדר, plants have sprouted enough that forbidden mixtures can be noticed.

phrases.english: but regarding the shekels, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא עַל הַכִּלְאַיִם דִּזְמַן זְרִיעָה הִיא אֶלָּא עַל הַשְּׁקָלִים מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the timing of the two announcements listed in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source or reason for announcing the שקלים on the first of אדר?

steps.title: The verse teaches that offerings must come from the new collection
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבי, quoting רבי יאשיה, cites the פסוק 'זאת עולת חודש בחדשו.' It teaches that the Torah wants קרבנות brought from a new collection of funds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טבי said in the name of רבי יאשיה: The פסוק says, 'This is the burnt-offering of the month in its month.' The תורה is saying: renew, and bring an offering from the new collection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the שקלים timing. A פסוק teaches that at a certain point each year, the קרבנות must start being bought with newly collected money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בחדשו' (in its month) is read as a hint to 'חַדֵּשׁ', meaning renew. Each year there must be a fresh fund for communal קרבנות, called תרומה חדשה. Once a new year begins, the old year's money can no longer be used for these offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse (a פסוק in the Torah)
Renew, start fresh
The new collection, the fresh year's half-shekel fund
An offering brought in the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule behind the whole מצוה of the half-shekel: communal קרבנות each year are funded by that year's new collection.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Tavi said in the name of Rabbi Yoshiyah:
For the verse says: 'This is the burnt-offering of the month in its month' (Numbers 28:14),
the Torah is saying: renew, and bring an offering
phrases.notes: 'בחדשו' is read as related to 'חדש', meaning new.

phrases.english: from the new collection.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the source for the שקלים announcement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'זאת עולת חודש בחדשו' teaches that communal קרבנות must be brought from a new year's collection, תרומה חדשה.

steps.title: Since new funds are needed by ניסן, the reading is moved up to אדר
steps.stepSummary: The new fund must be used starting in ניסן. So we read פרשת שקלים early, on the first of אדר, so that the שקלים reach the בית המקדש on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since in ניסן we need to bring offerings from the new collection, we read early, on the first of אדר, so that people will bring the שקלים to the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the פסוק to the calendar. It explains why the reminder comes a full month before ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The year for קרבנות begins in ניסן, which is learned elsewhere. From ניסן on, only new-collection money may be used. So the reminder must come in the month before, אדר, to give people time to give their half-shekel.

keyTerms.meaning: The month that begins the year for קרבנות and the new fund
We move it earlier
We read (פרשת שקלים)
So that / in order that

steps.whatToRemember: The announcement and the reading of פרשת שקלים happen on the first of אדר, because starting in ניסן, the קרבנות must be bought with the new half-shekel collection. The month of אדר gives people time to give.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק itself does not mention אדר. The פסוק only gives the rule of a new fund. The month of אדר is simply the practical lead time before ניסן.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דִּבְנִיסָן בָּעֵי אַקְרוֹבֵי מִתְּרוּמָה חֲדָשָׁה,
phrases.english: And since in Nisan one must offer from the new collection,
phrases.notes: The fact that the year for קרבנות starts in ניסן is learned elsewhere (ראש השנה 7a).

phrases.english: we move it early and read on the first of Adar,
so that they will bring shekels to the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דִּבְנִיסָן בָּעֵי אַקְרוֹבֵי מִתְּרוּמָה חֲדָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the source from step 3 to explain the אדר timing asked about in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because new-fund קרבנות begin in ניסן, the שקלים reminder and the reading of פרשת שקלים are moved up to the first of אדר, so the money arrives on time.

steps.title: The משנה seems not to follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה cannot follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, because he holds that preparing for a holiday begins only two weeks ahead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Because if it were like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, he said only two weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. Our משנה starts the שקלים announcement a full month before ניסן, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to need only two weeks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the announcement on the first of אדר prepares people for ניסן. But if, like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, preparation needs only two weeks, the announcement could wait until the middle of אדר. So the משנה looks like it goes against his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? (Whose opinion does this follow?)
Not like (this opinion)
Because if
But he said! (introduces a contradiction)
Two weeks

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן — דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: Like whom? Not like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
phrases.notes: The question 'like whom' is answered right away: at least not like him.

phrases.english: For if it were Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
didn't he say two weeks?
phrases.notes: In his view, two weeks of preparation is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן — דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reason from Step 4 (prepare for ניסן) and asks whether the one-month lead time fits every opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the שקלים announcement is made on the first of אדר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If preparation needs only two weeks (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל), there is no reason to announce a full month early.

steps.title: The ברייתא on studying the laws of פסח thirty days or two weeks before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as the source: the תנא קמא says we study the laws of פסח thirty days before, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says two weeks.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: We ask about the laws of פסח thirty days before פסח. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: two weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the claim in Step 5. It shows where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said that two weeks of preparation is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about learning הלכות פסח, but the גמרא treats it as a general measure of how early to prepare for a holiday. The first opinion (thirty days) fits the משנה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion (two weeks) seems not to fit it.

keyTerms.meaning: We ask and study (about the laws)
The laws of פסח
Thirty days

phrases.english: As it is taught: We inquire into the laws of Passover
thirty days before Passover.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: two weeks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source that backs up the problem raised in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds preparation begins only two weeks before
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about studying הלכות פסח

steps.title: Even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees, because the tables open on the fifteenth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל too. The collection tables open on the fifteenth of אדר, and two weeks before that is the first of אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The Master taught: on the fifteenth of אדר the money-changers' tables sit in the towns, and on the twenty-fifth they sit in the בית המקדש. Because of the tables, we read early.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 5 and shows the משנה can match רבן שמעון בן גמליאל after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real deadline is not ניסן. It is the fifteenth of אדר, when people can already start paying at the tables in the towns. Two weeks before the fifteenth is the first of אדר, which fits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's two-week rule exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (it follows this opinion)
Money-changers' tables for collecting the שקלים
The towns outside the בית המקדש
We read early

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a two-week preparation period is measured from when the obligation can first be fulfilled, here the opening of the tables, and not from ניסן.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
since the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בּוֹ שׁוּלְחָנוֹת יוֹשְׁבִין בַּמְּדִינָה
phrases.english: On its fifteenth day (of Adar), the tables are set up in the towns,
and on the twenty-fifth they are set up in the Temple.
Because of the tables, we read it early.
phrases.notes: Two weeks before the fifteenth is the first of אדר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from Steps 5 and 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the reference point: the deadline is the opening of the tables, not ניסן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two weeks are counted back from ניסן, so the announcement could wait until the middle of אדר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two weeks are counted back from the fifteenth of אדר, when the tables open, so the announcement belongs on the first of אדר.

steps.title: Which portion is פרשת שקלים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which Torah passage is read as פרשת שקלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is פרשת שקלים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic and asks a simple question. It is setting up the disagreement between רב and שמואל in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא has discussed when the reading happens. Now it asks what is actually read.

keyTerms.meaning: What is?
The special Torah reading about the שקלים

phrases.english: What is the portion of Shekalim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the timing of the reading to its content.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which Torah passage counts as פרשת שקלים

steps.title: רב says the daily offerings portion, שמואל says כי תשא
steps.stepSummary: רב says פרשת שקלים is "צו את בני ישראל... את קרבני לחמי" (the offerings, in במדבר כח). שמואל says it is "כי תשא" (שמות ל).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: "Command the children of Israel and say to them: My offering, My bread." שמואל said: "When you take the count."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two answers to the question. רב and שמואל disagree about which passage is read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל picks the passage that openly commands giving the half-שקל. רב picks the passage about the daily and מוסף offerings, which are the things the שקלים pay for.

keyTerms.meaning: "Command the children of Israel" (the offerings portion, בַּמִּדְבָּר כח)
My offering, My bread (the קָרְבָּנוֹת on the מִזְבֵּחַ)
"When you take the count" (שְׁמוֹת ל, the half-שֶׁקֶל command)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "צו את בני ישראל" here with פרשת צו in ויקרא. רב means the offerings passage in פרשת פנחס (במדבר כח). In practice, we follow שמואל and read "כי תשא."

phrases.english: Rav said: "Command the children of Israel
and say to them: My offering, My bread."
And Shmuel said: "When you take the count."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 8, with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: the offerings passage ("את קרבני לחמי"). שמואל: "כי תשא."

steps.title: שמואל's portion mentions שקלים, but רב's does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts שמואל's view, since "כי תשא" mentions the שקלים. It challenges רב: the offerings passage never mentions שקלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who said "כי תשא". That is why it is called פרשת שקלים, because שקלים are written in it. But for the one who said "את קרבני לחמי", are שקלים written there at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's opinion. If a portion is named פרשת שקלים, it should mention שקלים, and רב's portion does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name of the reading is used as a test. "כי תשא" passes because it speaks about the half-שקל. רב's passage only describes offerings, so it seems a strange choice for a reading called שקלים.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for one view); a challenge to the other view follows
According to the one who said
That is why
But (introduces the difficulty)
Is anything written there?

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who said "When you take the count,"
that is why it is called the portion of Shekalim,
because "shekels" is written in it.
But according to the one who said "My offering, My bread,"
is anything about "shekels" written there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's answer from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that פרשת שקלים is the offerings passage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reading named שקלים should mention שקלים, and רב's passage never does.

steps.title: רב's reading fits because of רבי טבי's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: yes, it fits. The reason שקלים are collected is רבי טבי's teaching, that the offerings must be bought from new funds, so the offerings passage is about what the שקלים pay for.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. What is the reason for collecting them? As רבי טבי taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. Even though the word שקלים is not in his passage, the passage is about the very purpose of the שקלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 3, רבי טבי taught that "עולת חודש בחדשו" requires the offerings to come from a new collection. So the שקלים exist to pay for these offerings. Reading the offerings passage reminds people why they need to give.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
What is the reason?
As (that רַבִּי) taught

steps.whatToRemember: פרשת שקלים is read at the start of אדר: on ראש חודש אדר itself when it falls on שבת, otherwise on the שבת just before it. Even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees to this timing, because the tables open on the fifteenth. רב says the reading is the offerings passage (since the שקלים pay for the offerings, per רבי טבי). שמואל says it is "כי תשא," which openly mentions the שקלים.

phrases.english: Yes. What is the reason (for collecting them)?
As Rabbi Tavi taught.
phrases.notes: The offerings must come from the new collection, so the offerings passage is about the purpose of the shekels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב from Step 10, using רבי טבי's teaching from Step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Connection through purpose: the passage describes what the שקלים pay for
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A reading called שקלים must actually contain the word שקלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: A passage about the offerings that the שקלים fund is a fitting reading for פרשת שקלים.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל: "כי תשא" is about sockets, not offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now flips the earlier question. רב's view fits, because the offerings passage lists the קרבנות that the שקלים pay for. But on שמואל's view, "כי תשא" only mentions שקלים used for the אדנים of the משכן, not for קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says the reading is "צו את בני ישראל": the offerings are written there, as רבי טבי explained. But for the one who says "כי תשא", are offerings written there? Only שקלים for the אדנים are written there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns around and challenges שמואל. The passage he picked talks about shekels for the sockets of the משכן, not shekels for buying קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רב was defended with רבי טבי's teaching that the offerings must be bought with new money, so the offerings passage connects to the שקלים. Now the problem is reversed. The Adar collection pays for קרבנות, but "כי תשא" describes a one-time collection for the אדנים. So why read it?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (this view works, but the other one is a problem)
According to the one who says
Are they written? (a challenging question)
The silver sockets that held up the boards of the משכן

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier (step 10) שמואל looked like the easy view and רב was the one challenged. Now the roles switch: רב is the comfortable view, and שמואל is the one under attack.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״צַו אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ —
phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who says "Command the children of Israel"
phrases.notes: This is רב's view.

phrases.english: because offerings are written there,
phrases.notes: The offerings bought with the שקלים are listed there.

phrases.english: as רבי טבי explained.
phrases.notes: The offerings must be bought from new funds (step 11).

phrases.english: But according to the one who says "When you take the count,"
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's view.

phrases.english: are offerings written there?
Shekels for the sockets are written there!
phrases.notes: That money built the משכן. It did not buy קרבנות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״כִּי תִשָּׂא״, ״קׇרְבָּנוֹת״ מִי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the challenge of step 10: after defending רב, the גמרא now attacks שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that פרשת שקלים is "כי תשא"

steps.title: רב יוסף: three separate contributions, one for the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רב יוסף's teaching. The word תרומה appears three times in "כי תשא", which teaches that there were three contributions. One was for the מזבח, one for the אדנים, and one for בדק הבית. So "כי תשא" does include shekels for קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף taught: there are three contributions. The altar's contribution is for the altar, the sockets' contribution is for the sockets, and the Temple-maintenance contribution is for Temple maintenance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. "כי תשא" is not only about the sockets, because it hints at a contribution for the מזבח too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף reads the three mentions of תרומה in the passage as three different collections. One of them, the contribution for the מזבח, is exactly what the yearly Adar collection pays for. So שמואל's passage does connect to קרבנות after all.

steps.title: Challenge to רב: what makes ראש חודש אדר's reading different?
steps.stepSummary: On שמואל's view, ראש חודש אדר clearly stands out: "כי תשא" is read instead of the usual ראש חודש passage. But on רב's view, the passage is "צו את קרבני", which is already read on every שבת ראש חודש. So what is special about this day?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says "כי תשא": that is how this ראש חודש is different from other ראשי חדשים. But for the one who says "צו את קרבני", what is different?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge against רב. If the special reading is the same passage read on any שבת ראש חודש, nothing seems to mark the day as special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every שבת ראש חודש already includes a reading from the offerings passage in במדבר כח. If פרשת שקלים is that same passage, it seems the reading adds nothing new. On שמואל's view there is a clear change, because a different passage is read.

steps.title: The difference: all seven read the ראש חודש passage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is a difference. On a normal שבת ראש חודש, six people read from the weekly portion and only one reads the ראש חודש passage. On ראש חודש אדר, all seven read from the ראש חודש passage.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. The passage may be the same, but the amount read is different, and that makes the day stand out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is not which passage is read but how much of the reading it takes up. On a regular שבת ראש חודש, the offerings passage gets only one עליה. On ראש חודש אדר it takes over all seven עליות, which marks the day as פרשת שקלים.

steps.title: The answer only works if the weekly portion is skipped
steps.stepSummary: Step 15's answer works for the view that on the four special שבתות the regular weekly portion is not read at all. But for the view that the regular portion is still read, ראש חודש אדר again looks the same as any שבת ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: That answer works for the one who says the משנה means we go back to the regular order of Torah portions. But for the one who says it means we go back to the regular order of הפטרות, and we still read the weekly portion, what is different about this day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions its own answer from step 15. It shows that the answer only works under one reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that on the fifth שבת we 'go back to the regular order'. One view says this means the regular Torah portions, so on the special שבתות the weekly portion was skipped completely, and all seven people could read the ראש חודש passage. The other view says it means the regular הפטרות, so the weekly portion was still read. Under that view, step 15's answer fails, and the question returns: how is ראש חודש אדר different?

steps.title: A ברייתא: the הפטרה is the story of יהוידע הכהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. When ראש חודש אדר falls on שבת, we read פרשת שקלים, and the הפטרה is the story of יהוידע הכהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: When ראש חודש אדר falls on שבת, we read פרשת שקלים, and the הפטרה is about יהוידע הכהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge by quoting a ברייתא. This step only sets up the source; the challenge itself is built in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us which הפטרה goes with פרשת שקלים: the story in מלכים where יהוידע הכהן collects money for repairing the בית המקדש. Since a הפטרה is supposed to match the Torah reading, this detail can help decide which passage פרשת שקלים is.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the הפטרה fits שמואל's view well. This sets up the coming question of how it could fit רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כי תשא' is about each person giving a half-shekel. The יהוידע story says 'כסף נפשות ערכו', money given per person, so the two clearly match. The unspoken point is that 'צו את קרבני', רב's passage, is about קרבנות, not collecting money. The full question against רב comes next.

steps.deeperAnalysis: A הפטרה is supposed to match the Torah reading. 'כי תשא' is about the half-shekel, so a הפטרה about collecting money for the מקדש fits it. 'את קרבני לחמי' is about the daily קרבנות, not about collecting money, so the match is unclear.

steps.title: Yes, in ארץ ישראל's three-year cycle

They complete the תורה reading
In three years

steps.whatToRemember: Both views of פרשת שקלים survive. The הפטרה fits 'את קרבני' because of רבי טבי, and the ברייתא about reading it twice fits 'את קרבני' because of ארץ ישראל's three-year cycle.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that in the times of the גמרא, ארץ ישראל followed a three-year Torah-reading cycle, different from the one-year cycle of בבל that we follow today.

phrases.english: Yes, for the people of the West
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.english: who complete the Torah in three years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a specific place and custom
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'את קרבני' is always read in the summer, so it can never be next to ראש חודש אדר.
steps.terutzMaskana: In ארץ ישראל's three-year cycle, 'את קרבני' can fall near אדר, so the ברייתא fits this view too.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל: פרשת שקלים is 'כי תשא'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that on ראש חודש אדר falling on שבת we read 'כי תשא' with the הפטרה of יהוידע הכהן. This matches שמואל's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with שמואל: When ראש חודש אדר falls on שבת, we read 'כי תשא', and the הפטרה is the story of יהוידע הכהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up שמואל in his argument with רב about which passage counts as פרשת שקלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said פרשת שקלים is 'צו את בני ישראל ... את קרבני לחמי', and שמואל said it is 'כי תשא'. This ברייתא names 'כי תשא' outright, and its הפטרה about יהוידע collecting money for the בית המקדש fits the half-shekel theme. So the ברייתא supports שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him (a supporting source)
'When you take the count' (שמות ל), the half-shekel passage
They read as the הפטרה (the reading from the נביאים)
יהוידע the כהן, who collected money to repair the בית המקדש (מלכים ב יב)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports שמואל: פרשת שקלים is 'כי תשא', and its הפטרה is יהוידע הכהן.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: When the New Moon of Adar falls on Shabbat,
they read 'When you take the count'
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's view of פרשת שקלים

phrases.english: and for the haftara they read the story of Jehoiada the priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the רב and שמואל debate by bringing a tannaitic source that supports שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that פרשת שקלים is 'כי תשא'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that names 'כי תשא' as the reading for ראש חודש אדר on שבת, with the הפטרה of יהוידע הכהן

steps.title: Three ספרי תורה on ראש חודש אדר that falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא rules that on ראש חודש אדר falling on שבת, three ספרי תורה are taken out: one for the weekly portion, one for ראש חודש, and one for 'כי תשא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא said: When ראש חודש אדר falls on שבת, we take out three ספרי תורה. From one we read the weekly portion of the day, from one the ראש חודש reading, and from one 'כי תשא'.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רבי יצחק נפחא, gives a practical rule about how many ספרי תורה to use when ראש חודש אדר falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three different readings come together on this one שבת: the regular weekly פרשה, the ראש חודש reading, and פרשת שקלים. Each reading gets its own ספר תורה. Because he names the third reading as 'כי תשא', he is following שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: They take out three ספרי תורה
The matter of the day, meaning the regular weekly פרשה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said:

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: When the New Moon of Adar falls on Shabbat,
they take out three Torah scrolls,

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹרִין בָּהֶן אֶחָד בְּעִנְיָינוֹ שֶׁל יוֹם,
phrases.english: and read from them: one for the regular reading of the day,
one for the New Moon reading,
and one for 'When you take the count.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the same case (ראש חודש אדר on שבת) and adds the rule about how many ספרי תורה to use.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש חודש אדר that falls on שבת, three ספרי תורה are used: the weekly portion, ראש חודש, and 'כי תשא'.

steps.title: Three ספרי תורה on ראש חודש טבת that falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא gives the same rule for ראש חודש טבת on שבת: the weekly portion, ראש חודש, and חנוכה, each from its own ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא also said: When ראש חודש טבת falls on שבת, we bring three ספרי תורה. From one we read the weekly portion of the day, from one the ראש חודש reading, and from one the חנוכה reading.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק נפחא gives a second, parallel rule. This time the case is ראש חודש טבת, which always falls during חנוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too three readings meet on one שבת: the weekly פרשה, ראש חודש, and חנוכה. So once again three separate ספרי תורה are used. Having two parallel rulings sets up the גמרא's next question: why did he need to say both?

keyTerms.meaning: The new month of טבת, which always falls during חנוכה
They bring (the ספרי תורה)
The reading for חנוכה (the נשיאים in פרשת נשא)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said:

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ טֵבֵת שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: When the New Moon of Tevet falls on Shabbat,
they bring three Torah scrolls,

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹרִין בָּהֶן אֶחָד בְּעִנְיָינוֹ שֶׁל יוֹם,
phrases.english: and read from them: one for the regular reading of the day,
one for the New Moon reading,
and one for Hanukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling by the same אמורא that follows the same three-scroll pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש חודש טבת that falls on שבת, three ספרי תורה are used: the weekly portion, ראש חודש, and חנוכה.

steps.title: Why both rulings of רבי יצחק were needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both rulings are needed. From the טבת ruling alone, we might have thought that for אדר רבי יצחק holds like רב, so two ספרי תורה would be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If he had only said the rule about טבת, we might think רבי יצחק says it only there. But about אדר, we might think he holds like רב, who said פרשת שקלים is 'את קרבני לחמי', and then two ספרי תורה would be enough. So he teaches us that even for אדר we use three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יצחק needed to state the אדר ruling even though he also stated the טבת ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, פרשת שקלים is 'את קרבני לחמי' (פרשת פנחס), and that same passage is also the ראש חודש reading. So under רב one ספר could cover both, and two ספרי תורה would be enough. The אדר ruling tells us רבי יצחק holds like שמואל ('כי תשא'), so a third ספר is truly needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (to state both rulings)
He holds like רב
'My offering, My bread' (במדבר כח), רב's פרשת שקלים
It is enough
He teaches us (something new)

steps.confusionAlert: 'בהא' here means טבת and 'בהך' means אדר. The worry is that under רב, the ראש חודש reading and פרשת שקלים are the same passage, so they could be read from one ספר.

phrases.english: And it is necessary to state both,
for if it had been said only about this case (Tevet),
I would say that only here does Rabbi Yitzchak say it,
but about that case (Adar), he holds like Rav,
who said the Shekalim portion is 'My offering, My bread,'
and two Torah scrolls are enough,
phrases.notes: Because that passage is also the ראש חודש reading

phrases.english: so he teaches us that three are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why both rulings were said.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Necessity (צריכותא): each ruling teaches something the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the טבת ruling alone, we would think that for אדר רבי יצחק follows רב, so two ספרי תורה would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אדר ruling shows that רבי יצחק follows שמואל, so three ספרי תורה are needed.

steps.title: Then let him state only the Adar case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the אדר ruling is the one with the new point, why was the טבת ruling needed at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him say this one (אדר), and he would not need that one (טבת)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the explanation it just gave. It asks why the טבת ruling was needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If three ספרי תורה are needed for אדר even though רב's view might have let us get by with two, then טבת is obviously three. In טבת all three readings are clearly different passages. So the טבת ruling seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him say this one
And that one would not be needed

phrases.english: But let him say this one (Adar),
and that one (Tevet) would not be needed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the necessity explanation of step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that both rulings of רבי יצחק were needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אדר ruling is the harder case, so the טבת ruling follows from it automatically and seems unnecessary.

steps.title: One ruling was learned from the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יצחק only said the אדר ruling. The טבת ruling was learned from it by others.
steps.simpleTranslation: One was said by inference from the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the challenge. It explains that רבי יצחק never said the טבת ruling himself; students learned it from his אדר ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no claim that he taught two separate rulings. He said only the אדר rule, and the טבת rule was reported as his because it follows from it. This removes the question of why both were said.

keyTerms.meaning: One was stated by inference from the other

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק נפחא said: three ספרי תורה on ראש חודש אדר that falls on שבת (following שמואל's 'כי תשא'). The same rule for ראש חודש טבת and חנוכה was learned from it.

phrases.english: One was stated by inference from the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 30 by accepting it: only one ruling was actually said.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the challenge and changes how the source is described (only one ruling was really stated)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יצחק stated two separate rulings, so each must teach something new.
steps.terutzMaskana: He stated only the אדר ruling, and the טבת ruling was learned from it.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: Three read ראש חודש, one reads חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: A new dispute is introduced. When ראש חודש טבת falls on a weekday, רבי יצחק rules that three people read the ראש חודש portion and one reads the חנוכה portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: When ראש חודש טבת falls on a weekday, רבי יצחק said: three people read from the ראש חודש portion, and one reads from the חנוכה portion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new dispute about a weekday ראש חודש טבת. This first half gives רבי יצחק's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps dealt with שבת, where more than one ספר תורה was taken out. Here it is a weekday, so there are four readers in total, and the question is how to split them between ראש חודש and חנוכה. רבי יצחק gives ראש חודש the main share of three readers.

keyTerms.meaning: The new month of טבת, which always falls during the days of חנוכה.
On a weekday, not on שבת.
Three people read from the Torah.
And one person.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier steps about שבת. On a weekday there are only four readers in total. The only question is how to divide those four readers between the ראש חודש reading and the חנוכה reading.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rosh Chodesh Tevet
that falls on a weekday,
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
three read from the Rosh Chodesh portion,
and one reads from the Chanukah portion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ טֵבֵת שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the שבת cases of רבי יצחק to a new weekday case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a weekday ראש חודש טבת, three people read ראש חודש and one reads חנוכה.

steps.title: רב דימי: Three read חנוכה, one reads ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי of חיפה disagrees and rules the opposite: three people read חנוכה and one reads ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב דימי of חיפה said: three people read from the חנוכה portion, and one reads from the ראש חודש portion.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second side of the dispute. רב דימי flips רבי יצחק's split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי gives חנוכה the main share of three readers and leaves only the fourth reader for ראש חודש. Both sides agree there are four readers. They argue only about which reading is primary.

keyTerms.meaning: In the חנוכה portion (the offerings of the נשיאים).

phrases.english: And Rav Dimi of Haifa said:
three read from the Chanukah portion,
and one reads from the Rosh Chodesh portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי יצחק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a weekday ראש חודש טבת, three people read חנוכה and one reads ראש חודש.

steps.title: רבי מני supports רבי יצחק: the frequent practice comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני argues that logic favors רבי יצחק, because of the rule that when a frequent practice and an infrequent practice compete, the frequent one comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני said: It makes sense to follow רבי יצחק נפחא, because when there is something frequent and something not frequent, the frequent one comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני gives a reason to side with רבי יצחק. He uses the well-known principle of תדיר קודם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראש חודש comes every month, while חנוכה comes only once a year. So ראש חודש is the more frequent practice (תדיר) and deserves the main reading of three people.

keyTerms.meaning: Like him; in agreement with his opinion.
It stands to reason; it makes logical sense.
Between something frequent and something infrequent, the frequent one comes first.
The blacksmith. This is a nickname of רבי יצחק.

steps.whyThisMatters: תדיר קודם is a general rule used all over ש״ס, for example in deciding which קרבן or which מצוה comes first. Here it is applied to the order and weight of Torah readings.

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani said:
It stands to reason to follow Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha,
for between a frequent practice and an infrequent one,
the frequent one comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Weighs in on the dispute in favor of רבי יצחק.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's ruling that three people read ראש חודש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The general principle תדיר ושאינו תדיר, תדיר קודם.

steps.title: רבי אבין supports רב דימי: ראש חודש caused the fourth reader
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין argues that logic favors רב דימי. The fourth reader is only added because of ראש חודש, so the fourth reader should read ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said: It makes sense to follow רב דימי. What caused the fourth reader to come? ראש חודש. Therefore the fourth reader should read the ראש חודש portion.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין gives a reason to side with רב דימי. He argues that ראש חודש is the reason there is a fourth reader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the other days of חנוכה only three people read, all from חנוכה. The extra fourth reader exists only because it is ראש חודש. So that added reader should read ראש חודש, and the usual three stay with חנוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: What caused it?
For the fourth reader to come.
Therefore.
He needs to read.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said:
It stands to reason to follow Rav Dimi,
what caused the fourth reader to come?
Rosh Chodesh;

phrases.aramaic: הִלְכָּךְ רְבִיעִי בְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ בָּעֵי מִיקְרֵי.
phrases.english: therefore the fourth should read from Rosh Chodesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing logical argument, this time supporting רב דימי.
steps.raayaObject: רב דימי's ruling that only the fourth reader reads ראש חודש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reasoning that ראש חודש is what added the fourth reader.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final conclusion on this dispute is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by asking for the final הלכה after hearing both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side now has a solid logical argument. So the גמרא asks how we actually rule in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: What was concluded about it? A request for the final ruling.

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a final decision between the two sides.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה follows רבי יצחק or רב דימי.

steps.title: רב יוסף and רבה each take a side
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says we disregard ראש חודש as the main reading, like רב דימי. רבה says we disregard חנוכה as the main reading, like רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: We do not give priority to ראש חודש. And רבה said: We do not give priority to חנוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two later אמוראים answer the question, but they still disagree. Each one sides with a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's "we pay no attention to ראש חודש" means ראש חודש does not get the main reading, which matches רב דימי. רבה's "we pay no attention to חנוכה" means חנוכה does not get the main reading, which matches רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not pay attention to it, meaning we do not treat it as the main reading.

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "אין משגיחין ב..." names the reading that LOSES the main spot. So רב יוסף, who says אין משגיחין בראש חודש, actually holds like רב דימי.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
we do not give priority to Rosh Chodesh,
and Rabba said:
we do not give priority to Chanukah,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question, but with two opposing rulings.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף follows רב דימי; רבה follows רבי יצחק.

steps.title: Final הלכה: ראש חודש is the main reading
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רבה: we do not give priority to חנוכה, and ראש חודש is the main reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: we do not give priority to חנוכה, and ראש חודש is the main reading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling. Three people read ראש חודש and the fourth reads חנוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the dispute in favor of רבה, and so in favor of רבי יצחק and רבי מני's reasoning of תדיר קודם. ראש חודש, being the more frequent practice, gets the primary reading.

keyTerms.meaning: And the halacha is; the final practical ruling.
The main, primary part.

steps.whatToRemember: On a weekday ראש חודש טבת, three people read the ראש חודש portion and the fourth reads the חנוכה portion, because ראש חודש is more frequent (תדיר קודם).

phrases.english: And the halacha is: we do not give priority to Chanukah,
and Rosh Chodesh is primary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between רב יוסף and רבה in favor of רבה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ראש חודש is the main reading: three read ראש חודש and one reads חנוכה, following רבי יצחק.

steps.title: שקלים on the week of תצוה: six read תצוה, one reads שקלים
steps.stepSummary: A new case is introduced: פרשת שקלים falls on the Shabbat of ואתה תצוה. רבי יצחק נפחא rules that six people read from תצוה, and the seventh reads the שקלים section from כי תשא until ועשית. The line then opens אביי's response.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if it falls on the Shabbat of 'And you shall command' (תצוה), רבי יצחק נפחא said: six people read from 'And you shall command' until 'When you take' (כי תשא), and one reads from 'When you take' until 'And you shall make.' אביי said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It asks what to do when the special שקלים reading lands on the week of תצוה, and רבי יצחק נפחא gives his answer. The last words, 'אביי said,' set up the next move, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually seven people read the regular weekly portion, and the special reading is added separately. Here רבי יצחק נפחא uses the first six readers for the weekly portion תצוה and gives the seventh reader the שקלים section. This works because the שקלים section (the start of כי תשא) comes right after the end of תצוה in the same scroll, so the reader can simply keep going.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It falls on.' Used when a special day or reading lands on a particular date or Shabbat.
The special reading about the half-shekel (שמות ל:יא–טז), read around ראש חודש אדר.
The weekly portion תצוה. Its first words are 'And you shall command.'
'When you take [the count].' The start of the next portion, which is also the שקלים section.
'And you shall make' (the copper laver). This marks where the שקלים section ends.

steps.confusionAlert: 'כי תשא' here does not mean the whole weekly portion of כי תשא. It means only its opening section about the half-shekel, from 'כי תשא' up to 'ועשית כיור.' The words 'until כי תשא' mean up to that point but not including it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a practical question about dividing the Torah reading when the special reading sits right next to the weekly portion. אביי is about to react to this ruling.
